newsitem.title: UK: Syria's Assad was in coma-British newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Syria's Assad was in coma-British newspaper.

text.p: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad fell into a coma late last year and was revived by Russian doctors in January, a British weekly newspaper reported on Sunday.
Quoting government sources in Damascus, the Sunday Times said Assad spent two weeks in a coma. Officially, Assad went into hospital for surgery to treat a prostate problem.
"Sources in Damascus say the 66-year-old president collapsed in late December and spent two weeks in a coma," it said.

"His collapse put his doctors into a panic and Russian experts were flown to his bedside. Assad last week was said to be making a slow recovery. He has appeared in public looking pale and weak," the paper said.
It added: "Damascus has been abuzz with rumours about who will succeed Assad and there are fears that traditional rivalries could erupt in a bloody struggle for power once he dies.
